target: plant cell (PO_0009002) as part of costa (PO_0030072): bearer plant cell, whole/container costa (pattern 12 or count container)
reason: Cells of the bryophyte leaf midrib. PO has costa (PO_0030072, non-vascular leaf midrib) and plant cell; 'cell' alone was rejected only because it lacked its organ, which is named here. 'ventral/median/dorsal' are layers of the costa (guide cells, stereids) and stay as context, not new classes.

Generic small tooth: it needs the organ it belongs to (leaf margin, calyx, fruit, peristome...). Same as the 2026-11-13 decisions on horn, mucro and lobule. Where the organ is a leaf, leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518) applies through the margin rule.

A lobe of a lobe of an unnamed organ (pinnule lobes, leaf lobes, petal lobes). Generic part, like 'lateral lobe' and 'lobule' in the previous review. Counts ('with 1-3 secondary lobes') need the lobed organ as container.

target: length towards filament (PO_0009067), pattern 10 (ratio to another part)
reason: This is the comparison target in 'anthers 1/4-1/2 filament length': a dimension of the filament, not a part. The bearer is the anther and the quality is decreased length towards filament with the ratio bounds. The 'amount' readings are wrong.
Generic projecting rim or wing (equatorial flange of seeds or fruits, flanges of spores, stem flanges). It needs the organ it belongs to, like wing, ridge and crest in the previous review.

label: corpusculum
parent: is_a PO_0025496 multi-tissue plant structure; part_of FLOPO_0986051 gynostegium
definition: A hard, dark, clip-like body secreted by the stigma head of the gynostegium that, together with two translator arms, joins the pollinia of adjacent anthers into a pollinarium and attaches it to a pollinator. Found in Apocynaceae subfamily Asclepiadoideae.
reason: A distinct structure described with its own size, shape and colour in milkweed treatments. It is not the orchid viscidium (FLOPO_0986032), which comes from the rostellum. FLOPO already has the related classes pollinium and gynostegium. Propose it to PO upstream together with pollinarium and translator arm.

label: elater
parent: is_a PO_0009002 plant cell; part_of PO_0025094 sporangium
definition: An elongated, sterile cell with spiral wall thickenings that lies among the spores in the capsule of a liverwort or hornwort. It twists as it dries and so helps to disperse the spores.
reason: Real and frequently described in bryophyte floras (colour, number of spiral bands, free or attached). PO has no class. The Equisetum 'elaters' are spore-wall bands rather than cells, so the definition is limited to bryophytes, or a sibling class could be added. Propose to PO upstream.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) as part of leaf lamina (PO_0020039), or of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075) in bryophyte floras: bearer plant cell, whole the lamina
reason: Almost all examples are moss laminal cells (isodiametric, hexagonal, papillose, quadrate). The patterns can express this as a cell that is part of the lamina. Which whole applies depends on the flora (bryophyte or vascular). 'distal' and 'lower part' are region context.

A position in a series ('outer 5', 'outer 3 sepals', 'les extérieurs'). The part itself (sepal, phyllary, tepal) is elided or comes next. This is a fragment of a position phrase and could become a bearer_quality context word together with its noun.

label: trigone
parent: part_of GO:0009505 plant-type cell wall; part_of PO_0009002 plant cell
definition: A thickening of the plant cell wall at the corner where three or more cells meet, seen as a triangular thickening between the cell lumens. Characteristic of the leaf cells of many liverworts.
reason: A standard character in liverwort keys (absent, small, large, bulging) across 4 floras. It is subcellular, so it belongs to the cell wall and is outside PO's scope. Keep it in FLOPO or propose it to GO, not to PO.

Narrower: a vein of intermediate strength running between and parallel to the secondary veins (Manual of Leaf Architecture). It is neither secondary nor tertiary, so it maps to the parent leaf lamina vein, as was done for basal vein and veinlet.

The margin of a lobe of an unnamed organ (leaf, liverwort leaf lobe, keel, labellum). Both 'lobe' and 'margin' are generic without their organ (see the previous review). Where the clause names the leaf, leaf lamina lobe (PO_0025517) plus the margin region applies.
Exact: leaf blade is a synonym of leaf lamina, and 'leaf lobe' already maps to PO_0025517 in reviewed_local_bearers.tsv.

The middle lobe of an organ that is not named: orchid labellum, corolla lip, leaf, staminode. Same as 'lateral lobe' in the previous review. When the whole is labellum, labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028) applies through the organ.

This phrase names the container of a count ('flowers 4-5 per head'), not a part. It matches 'per node', 'per flower' and 'per cluster' from the previous review. 'head' already maps to capitulum inflorescence.

target: scale leaf (PO_0006003) as part of bulb (PO_0025356): bearer scale leaf, whole/container bulb
reason: Bulb scales are the scale leaves (cataphylls) or swollen leaf bases of a bulb. 'Bulb of 2 scales' is a count of scale leaves with container bulb. Fibrous outer coats are better read as tunic (FLOPO_0986041).

label: clinandrium
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of FLOPO_0986015 gynostemium
definition: The concave region at the apex of the orchid column, below and behind the anther, in which the anther rests. Its margin is often raised into a hood or wing.
reason: A named orchid structure with its own margin, indumentum and hood characters in 4 floras. Reading it as 'apex of gynostemium' would lose the hood and margin meaning. FLOPO already holds gynostemium, so propose both to PO upstream.

This is a pipeline artifact: 'phyll.' or 'phyllaries' was expanded twice. It means phyllary, which is a NARROW synonym of involucral bract (rule C250). The expansion bug should also be fixed at its source.

A position adjective whose noun (awn, papillae, lobes, flowers) follows or is elided ('4 apical'). Same as 'basal' and 'lateral' in the previous review. The region reading is already the 'apically' context word.

Narrower or related: these are bryophyte asexual propagules (filamentous, fusiform, leaf-like, in leaf axils), which are gemmae in the broad sense. PO's gemma definition restricts it to propagules borne on a thallus, so ask PO upstream to widen it to leafy bryophytes. Do not use fruit (PO_0009001), where 'propagule' is a synonym.

A wrong singular form of calli. 'callus' and 'calli' were already rejected as generic parts that need their organ (labellum, petal claw, lemma). Do not use PO_0005052 plant callus, which is undifferentiated tissue. Fix the singular form in the pipeline.

label: dorsal lamina
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0025075 non-vascular leaf
definition: The single-layered wing of a Fissidens leaf that lies on the abaxial side of the costa, opposite the vaginant lamina, and runs from the leaf apex towards the insertion.
reason: A key character in all Fissidens treatments (decurrent, rounded, narrowed at the base). It has siblings, the vaginant and apical laminae. It is genus-specific, so keep it in FLOPO for now and propose it to PO only together with its sibling classes.
Narrower: a coccus is a one-seeded mericarp of a lobed schizocarp or coccarium (Euphorbiaceae, Malvaceae, Rutaceae). PO's mericarp covers it.
An adjective (quality), not a structure. The noun 'horn' was rejected as generic. The statements say that some organ's apex bears a horn, which needs that organ.

label: endostome basal membrane
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0030042 peristome
definition: The continuous, membranous lower part of the inner peristome (endostome) of a moss capsule, from which the endostome segments and cilia arise.
reason: A standard moss peristome character (height relative to the exostome, number of cell rows, smooth or papillose) across 4 floras. PO has peristome and peristome tooth but no endostome parts. Propose it to PO upstream together with endostome and its segments.

target: phyllome lamina lobe (PO_0025514) as part of bract (PO_0009055); counts use container bract
reason: Lobes of a divided bract ('segments 3, sessile, obovate'). PO's phyllome lamina lobe applies to bracts, which are phyllomes, and part_of bract qualifies it.

label: leaf vein axil
parent: is_a PO_0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO_0020039 leaf lamina
definition: The region of the leaf lamina in the angle between the midvein and a secondary vein that branches from it, often bearing hairs or domatia.
reason: Floras give qualities of this region itself (barbate, pubescent). PO axil (PO_0025224) is the angle between a leaf and the stem, so it does not fit. Dome-shaped or foveate pits are domatia (FLOPO_0986021) and should go there. Propose it to PO upstream.
A wrong singular form of the quality 'inconspicuous'. The counted part is the noun that follows (veins, ribs, transverse veins). Fix the singular form in the pipeline.

Exact in PO: 'hermaphrodite flower' and 'perfect flower' are synonyms of flower. For counts, the flower is the bearer. 'bisexual' (and ☿) could be added as a bearer_quality context word beside male and female.
The container phrase of a count ('2-4 in a cluster'). 'cluster' and 'per cluster' were rejected before because the cluster's kind (fascicle, glomerule, cyme) is not stated.
